claims.text: Nearly 80% of the 71 primary articles reviewed on LLMs in computing education were published in the first 8 months of 2023.
The performance and capabilities of current generative AI models on computing education datasets are rapidly improving.

evidence.description: Synthesise findings from 71 primary articles, nearly 80% of which have been published in the first 8 months of 2023.
Benchmark the performance of several current GenAI models/tools on various computing education datasets, and highlight the extent to which the capabilities of current models are rapidly improving.

methodologies.name: Systematic Literature Review
methodologies.description: A review synthesising research findings from primary articles on large language models in computing education.
datasets: 71 primary articles on LLMs in computing education

methodologies.name: Global Attitude Survey
methodologies.description: A cross-national survey capturing attitudes of computing students and instructors toward GenAI/LLMs.

methodologies.name: Qualitative Educator Interviews
methodologies.description: In-depth qualitative interviews exploring pedagogical adaptations to generative AI.

methodologies.name: Ethical Analysis Framework
methodologies.description: Framing discussions on ethics and policy advice for computing education using an established code of ethics.
conditions: Framed using the ACM Code of Ethics

methodologies.name: Model Benchmarking
methodologies.description: Benchmarking generative AI models and tools on domain-specific computing education datasets.
conditions: Evaluated on multiple current GenAI models and tools
